tempo_in_sample.what: TEMPO, the development design. IN-SAMPLE and FITTED (thresholds chosen on it); never a generalisation estimate.
tempo_in_sample.honesty_table_arm_note: IN-SAMPLE: TEMPO is the development design and every threshold was chosen on it; folded in from a harness run record (python -m tools.s3.run --design tempo --permutations K), not re-run here

corpus_holdout_out_of_sample.what: the synthetic corpus holdout, published BEFORE the freeze as out/s3/honesty/holdout_rates.json: the only pre-published out-of-sample estimate.
corpus_holdout_out_of_sample.aggregation: one item per structure-kind truth register, except a synchronizer register of a declared chain unit, which is counted through its unit, plus one item per declared structure-kind unit; found = matched a harness-verified structure of an accepted kind at IoU > 0.5; exact = equal flop sets and verified; both libraries pooled (a design contributes twice). This is review[2]'s own aggregation, and the one every published holdout figure has used.

split.rule: tools/s3/corpus.py splits(): per (cohort, family), sha256(name) order, the first (n + 1) // 4 held out, then every corpus.FITTED_ON design forced into train; corpus.DROPPED designs are not in the corpus at all. docs/S3_DESIGN.md section 4.4 states the same rule and the in-sample / out-of-sample protocol.

caveats: The corpus is SYNTHETIC and was written by the same project as the recognizer; several of its classes (cohort 2) were added because the generalisation regression set showed them missing (changes.jsonl C23, C31). It is the best out-of-sample estimate that survives this round, not an independent one.

The generalisation regression sets (out/s3/review_generalisation, review_generalisation2) are NO LONGER held out: counter.py, lfsr.py, shift.py, controls.py and verify.py all consulted them (changes.jsonl C25).

TEMPO is the development design: every TEMPO figure is in-sample. Four recognizer fixes were traced from TEMPO misses by truth name (changes.jsonl C27-C30), and PC03, PC06, PC07, PC09, C01-C06, C10 and C21(d) were selected on TEMPO.
These rates come from ONE seeded corpus evaluation; they carry no confidence interval.

They describe the recognizer AND the harness verifier as of source.code_sha256: 'found' means the harness verified the structure, so a change to tools/s3/verify.py moves them as surely as a change to a recognizer module (review[1] issue 2).

THE false_positive_structures COLUMN OVERSTATES; found / exact and their denominators do NOT. out/s3/review_generalisation2/evaluate.py's outcomes() builds its item list from truth registers whose kind is in STRUCTURE_KINDS, so a 'flag' register's alt_kinds are never consulted. Under the truth's TOGGLE_RULE a 1-bit toggle is kind 'flag' with alt_kinds ['counter'] -- the truth EXPLICITLY ACCEPTS a counter over it -- yet such a prediction matches no item there and is scored a false positive. Counted on the evaluation this document was derived from, as false-positive structures of width 1 lying entirely in one truth register of kind 'flag': holdout 2 of 6, train 10 of 16. The overstatement is in the CONSERVATIVE direction. tools/s3/score.py -- the scorer every published table comes from -- does not make this error: score.Truth builds accepts from alt_kinds for EVERY truth register, a flag included. The scoring rule is left as it is on purpose: changing it would move a published out-of-sample number without a lead decision (changes.jsonl T04, T14).

comparison_against_the_two_pre_published.how_to_read: THREE DIFFERENT THINGS, never to be merged. (1) TEMPO is the fitted DEVELOPMENT design: IN-SAMPLE. (2) the synthetic corpus holdout is the OUT-OF-SAMPLE estimate published BEFORE the freeze (out/s3/honesty/holdout_rates.json, created 2026-09-23T05:32:33+00:00, freeze commit 232cfe6). (3) the blind set is the FIRST TRUE OUT-OF-SAMPLE test: 10 third-party designs drawn with the freeze seed. The puzzle is frozen-code-but-KNOWN and is not a generalisation estimate of any kind.
comparability_warnings: THE HOLDOUT'S 'found' IS A VERIFIED RATE. holdout_rates.json's own aggregation string: "found = matched a harness-verified structure of an accepted kind at IoU > 0.5; exact = equal flop sets and verified". So holdout.found_rate must be put beside the blind set's VERIFIED found recall, not beside its all-structures found recall. The all-structures comparator is DERIVED HERE as (found + found_unverified) / items from the document's own columns; it is not a number the document publishes.

DIFFERENT ITEM SETS. The holdout counts one item per structure-kind truth register (a synchronizer register of a declared chain unit counted through its unit) PLUS one item per declared structure-kind unit. The blind figures here are score.py's register denominators (tools/s3/score.py Truth.denominators: the truth registers of the kind, identical in strict and lenient). The two denominators are not the same object; holdout_rates.py says so itself ("the two are NOT comparable" of its own two aggregations).

DIFFERENT POPULATIONS. The holdout is 40 SYNTHETIC designs written by this project (its own caveat: "the best out-of-sample estimate that survives this round, not an independent one"); the blind set is 10 real third-party Tiny Tapeout designs.

The holdout rates come from ONE seeded evaluation and carry NO confidence interval (its own caveat). The Clopper-Pearson intervals given below for the BLIND rates are computed here, are not in any record, and assume independent registers -- registers inside one design are not independent, so they are an optimistic floor on the true uncertainty, not a finished inference.
